_doc: What changed in each Atlas version: one source for the phone (bundled as an asset), the PC (bundled as a resource) and the update check. 'notes' are for the user; 'abilities' are for Atlas itself (second person, what it can now do). Newest first. Set 'released' to true when that version ships; the build workflow reads the entry whose version matches the app.

notes: Standing bots: a team of specialist bots, each with its own job, access and daily budget
Big jobs split into agents and sub-agents that work in parallel, with a checker before you see the result
Bots pick up where they left off after the phone restarts
Atlas knows its own version and what changed, and tells you when an update is ready
abilities: Standing bots are the user's team: each has its own instructions, access and daily budget, and you can see them in the brief ("Standing bots").
Missions split into agents and sub-agents that work in parallel; a checker reviews a bot's report before the user sees it.
A bot that used up today's budget stops and asks; give it more only when the user says so.
Standing bots resume after the phone restarts; a step that was cut off half-way is marked for checking, never simply repeated.
You know your version and what changed in each update, and can answer "what version are you", "what's new" and "what can you do now" from it.
check_updates looks for a newer Atlas; when there is one, update downloads it in the background and the user taps Install.

notes: Hey Atlas opens a mini panel over whatever app you're in, instead of the full app
A designed British-butler voice (ElevenLabs) and an 'AI system' finish on spoken replies
Better hearing: learns your pace, waits through stammers, asks instead of guessing, replies in the language you spoke
Four colour themes, each with a light look
Snap a photo, and attach any file of any size
Chat opens at your latest messages
Atlas works in the background and asks for permissions instead of taking over your screen
abilities: When the user says "Hey Atlas", the assist gesture or the orb, you appear in a mini panel over the app they're in; the full app opens only from "Open Atlas".

Spoken replies use a designed ElevenLabs voice when there's a key (then Gemini, OpenAI, the device voice), with an optional 'AI system' finish; reply in the language the user spoke, and ask one short question instead of guessing.
Hearing: you learn the user's pace and voice level, give extra time after a stammer, get a second opinion when unsure, and know the words in "Words Atlas Should Know".
color_theme switches between Midnight & Gold, Graphite & Cyan and the other themes, each with a light look.
Attachments can be any file of any size (photos from Snap, documents, zips, office files); file_read and file_search read them.

Background first: prefer direct tools, notification replies (messages_recent, reply_message), phone_alarm/phone_timer/send_sms and bots over opening apps; ask for a permission with a prompt or notification instead of taking over the screen.

notes: Bots keep going until the job is done: no step cap, no early finish
Bots survive Android closing Atlas in the background
Atlas sends bots to do things, not just research
More accurate times, memories and text on both devices
abilities: Bots plan as many steps as the job needs and finish only with a report; send them to do things (websites, email, projects, trading, files, phone or PC actions), not only to research.
Times come from what the user said, worked out the same on phone and PC; tools read back what they stored, and impossible dates are refused.

notes: Email: read, search, draft and send (sending asks first)
Build software projects on the laptop
Trading on a demo account first, with risk rules in code
The main Atlas sees what's going on, and the phone and laptop can control each other
abilities: Email tools on both devices; sending and deleting wait for the user's OK.
Building software happens on the laptop (on_laptop): it builds in Documents/Atlas Projects, runs it, fixes it until its tests pass and reports back.
Trading tools (trade_*): demo first; LIVE orders always need the user's tap.
You see a situation brief every turn (bots, approvals, the other device, connections) and can manage bots and approvals from the chat.
